To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of speculative equilbria requires: (i) the fundamental value of the asset is not perfectly correlated with the private information of the agents, (ii) the private information is not perfectly correlated across agents, (iii) the private information has a finite range, (iv) the private information does not depend on the fundamental value of an asset and (v) the agents have a finite range of strategies, i.e. they do not bid the asset at any price.

the existence of a speculative equilibrium in an economy with a finite number of agents is a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a rational expectations equilibrium in an economy in which agents are infinitely lived and the number of agents is infinite.

(1) the existence of speculative equi- libria is proven; (2) in equilibrium all agents bid assets in increasing functions of private infor- mation which is uncor- related with the fundamental value of the asset; and (3) speculative information is valuable in equilibrium.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the existence of speculative equilbria is a consequence of the fact that the fundamental value is uncorrelated from private information, that the fundamental value has a finite support, that the agents are infinitely lived, and that the agents are risk neutral.
the existence of speculative equilbria in the overlapping generation model is a direct result of the assumption of increasing functions.
the equilibrium of the economy is a speculative equilibrium in which the fundamental value of the asset is a martingale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the existence of speculative equilbria in which agents have private information about the dividend stream and that this information is valuable.
speculative information can be valuable even when it does not help in predicting the dividend stream of the asset.
the existence of a speculative equilibrium is a consequence of a particular structure of the economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of speculative equilbria is not dependent upon the agents having rational expectations, or even being able to form rational expectations.
speculative information is not only valuable in equilibrium, but also that it is valuable for agents to bid according to increasing functions in private information.
the equilibrium concept is not a necessary ingredient for the existence of speculative bubbles.
